scene.note: Your functions read and write the files other programs use: CSV rows from the spreadsheet, and JSON that keeps lists and dictionaries.

steps.note: Dougie's spreadsheet saves the kit list, a heading row first.
The csv module reads each row as a list of texts, quotes taken care of.
The heading row is left out, and the first value of every other row is kept.
Each row comes as a dictionary keyed by the headings, every value text.
Each count is turned into a number before it is compared with the line.
The items below the line come back, in the order of the file.
The store is a dictionary of each kind and its count.
A heading row goes first, then a row for each kind, quotes added where a name needs them.
The spreadsheet can open the file again, in the same shape.
The store has to last until tomorrow.
It is written into the file as JSON, in double quotes.
Whatever the file held before is replaced by the store.
The file holds each call sign with two numbers, east and north.
JSON has no tuples, so each position comes back as a list and is turned into a tuple.
Ailsa gets every team's last position, east first.
